reader.notes: Every single-object identification probed binds that object and reads and writes its storage (Y OF G, X OF G, C OF CV, Z, F-REC, T OF LN1, TOT OF CFG OF R1). The one failure seen, TOT OF CFG refused when B declares TOT (scope2.cob), arises because GR1's set omits the sum counter, so it is recorded on 1985-GR-X.1.3.8.2-1; once the set is right this rule's step holds.

refuter.evidence: Probe one1.cob (container ON1O: FD FA GLOBAL with 01 FREC. 05 FX; 01 G GLOBAL. 05 X; 01 CV GLOBAL 88 C. Contained ON1I declares its OWN FD FA (01 BREC), its own 01 G PIC X(3) and its own 01 CV PIC X, and writes MOVE 'QQQ' TO FX OF FREC OF FA): --std 85 EXIT 65, 'one1.cob(45,26): error COBOL1639: 'FX OF FREC OF FA' does not uniquely identify a data item - 'FX' is declared, but not under the given qualifiers (FREC OF FA)'. Over GR1's set (ON1I's names plus the container's global names: FA twice, FREC and FX once) the qualified reference FX OF FREC OF FA identifies exactly one object, the container's FX, so by GR2 it is the referenced object. The compiler applies that very reading to a data-name qualifier: one2.cob (the same program with that line replaced) runs EXIT 0 and prints 'I G=LOC / I XG=OUX / I C OF CV TRUE / I C TRUE / I FX= / O X=NEW': X OF G and C OF CV, whose qualifiers G and CV ON1I also declares, reach the container's single object. Only the file-name qualifier is decided by spelling first: SymbolTable.DataNameCandidates.cs#QualifierChainMatchesFrom asks SymbolTable.Files.cs#FileQualifies, which looks the qualifier up with FileNamed(..., NameReach.Visible); HideShadowedFiles (via InheritStep.DropShadowed) has already put the container's FA in _hiddenFileNames, so the lookup returns ON1I's own FA, whose Records do not hold FREC. The two qualifier arms cannot both be right under one reading of X.1.3.8.2: either G/CV must be refused or FA must qualify; GR1/GR2's text ('Using this set of names, the normal rules for qualification ... are applied until one or more objects is identified'; 'If only one object is identified, it is the referenced object') makes FA qualify. At --std 2023 the same refusal (one1-002, citing §2023:8.4.2.2). The reader's own sum counter case (TOT OF CFG) is the same mechanism (a spelling-based hide before qualification) in another name class; the reader booked it to GR1, but GR2's outcome fails on it as well. kb/Work: searched (FileQualifies, file-name qualifier, PB5786, PB3557): none owns a hidden GLOBAL file-name as a record qualifier. Citations: OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR1 ('the normal rules for qualification and any other rules for uniqueness of reference are applied until one or more objects is identified'); OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR2 ('If only one object is identified, it is the referenced object').
